title: Shakira and Burna Boy's World Cup Anthem 'Dai Dai' Is STILL the Biggest Song Outside the U.S.!
summary: Have you ever heard a song so catchy you couldn't stop humming it? That's what's happening around the world with 'Dai Dai,' the official song for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Shakira and Burna Boy made it, and it just stayed at number one for the second week in a row on a special chart called the Global Excl. U.S. — that's a list of the most popular songs everywhere EXCEPT the United States. A week ago, 'Dai Dai' made history as the first World Cup anthem to ever top that chart. The song was performed live in front of more than 80,000 fans at the World Cup opening ceremony in Mexico City. Can you picture that many people dancing and singing along? Meanwhile, Ariana Grande's song 'Hate That I Made You Love Me' climbed back to number one on the Global 200 chart, which counts streams and sales from the whole world, including the U.S. That's a big deal because it ties her record for the longest time at the top. The World Cup runs until July 19, and the closing show will be huge — Shakira, BTS, and Madonna are all performing at the first-ever halftime show during the final game! Other songs are still super popular too: BTS' 'Swim' is at number two, and a song by Ella Langley called 'Choosin' Texas' just hit the top five after 36 weeks — that's the longest climb ever for a female artist without any featured guests. So if you're looking for a new song to add to your playlist, 'Dai Dai' might just be the one everyone's dancing to this summer.
why_it_matters: This shows how music from different countries can bring people together, just like when you and your friends share favorite songs.

background_read: The FIFA World Cup is the biggest soccer tournament in the world, held every four years.
Shakira (a famous singer from Colombia) also performed the World Cup song 'Waka Waka' in 2010, which became a huge hit.
Burna Boy is a popular musician from Nigeria known for mixing African rhythms with pop music.
Article_Structure: WHAT: Their song 'Dai Dai' stayed number one on the Global Excl. U.S. chart for a second week.
WHERE: The chart tracks songs everywhere except the United States; the opening ceremony was in Mexico City.
WHY: The song is catchy and it is the first World Cup anthem to reach number one on this chart, showing its worldwide popularity.

perspectives.description: Fans and soccer lovers are excited because a World Cup song is topping the charts, showing that music connects people across the world.
Some might say that the Global Excl. U.S. chart ignores American listeners, so it doesn't show a song's full worldwide popularity.
The song's success reflects the huge interest in the World Cup, but chart rankings can change very quickly.
